rubrics.criterion: The number-theoretic factoring entry point in src/math/mod.rs is again a short driver over separately named sub-procedures, with the deterministic primality screen and the parameterized divisor search removed from its body and living in their own reusable units whose per-input behavior is unchanged (same ascending prime multisets, including for large composites such as 7156857700403137441).
rubrics.rationale: The factoring driver is the deepest absorbed call chain in this instance (driver -> screen -> modular leaves, plus the divisor walk and its gcd leaf); restoring independent, reusable units there is the core resolution for the number-theory component, independent of what names or signatures the solver chooses.

rubrics.criterion: The suffix array constructor in src/string_proc.rs no longer re-implements its stable counting stages (tally, running starts, scatter) twice inside its own body; ordering construction goes through one shared unit again and the constructor retains only its own rank-doubling loop logic.
rubrics.rationale: This constructor uniquely absorbs the same scratch-array stage at two successive applications; the instance-specific obligation is removing that duplicated stage from the constructor, not any particular decomposition of the doubling loop.

rubrics.criterion: In src/range_query/static_arq.rs, both the range-apply walk and the range-aggregate walk again delegate their pending-tag dispersal to dedicated sub-procedures, and the update walk no longer inlines per-node tag compose or ancestor re-aggregation; the two paths may share the restored units or use their own, as long as no walk duplicates those low-level pastes in its body.
rubrics.rationale: The write and read paths of this tree duplicated identical dispensing leaves; the obligation is specific to this component and deliberately allows several sound re-layerings (shared dispersal unit, restored per-level helper, or equivalent structure).

rubrics.criterion: In src/range_query/dynamic_arq.rs, the recursive range-apply walk again delegates child-arena allocation, persistence path cloning, pending-tag flush, and post-recursion aggregate recomposition to dedicated units, for both the total-overlap and partial-overlap regimes, instead of performing them inline at each recursion boundary.
rubrics.rationale: The persistent tree's absorbed bookkeeping is the arena-based variant of the same smell; the criterion names the four absorbed responsibilities and both regimes, without prescribing helpers matching any particular reference layout.

rubrics.criterion: Across all four files, every entry point that absorbed a multi-level helper subtree has been decomposed: no single remaining production function interleaves three or more formerly distinct pipeline stages (leaf arithmetic, propagation bookkeeping, and top-level traversal or ordering) in one undifferentiated body.
rubrics.rationale: This is the completion check for the whole instance: it grades the repair width (all absorbed entry points across math, string processing, and both tree variants) from the final source, without reference to how any single site was fixed.

rubrics.criterion: Restored sub-procedures are placed at the abstraction level their old collaborators used: sibling production paths of the same types that still need identical bookkeeping (for example the aggregate-merge and descriptor-walk units still used by other tree operations, or the primality screen used by the public prime test) call the reintroduced units rather than carrying their own private copies.
rubrics.rationale: The absorption deleted units that other surviving code paths also rely on; a repair that only serves the five absorbed entry points leaves the crate's helper layer split-brained, which this criterion catches.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave duplicate low-level implementations: each formerly duplicated leaf computation (the modular-arithmetic normalizing step, the stable scatter stage, the pending-tag compose block, the Euclid-style reduction, path cloning) exists once in the final crate, not once per paste site or once per module copy.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for this instance is extracting the repeated pastes five separate times into per-site private helpers, which moves the duplication but does not remove it; this criterion is answerable by inspection of the final source.

rubrics.criterion: The crate's public surface is untouched: no public function or method signature, module path, trait bound, documented panic condition, or validity contract (for example that an empty range l > r is legal and r >= size panics for the trees) changes, and helper units are private to their modules unless the pre-existing public API already exposed an equivalent.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed units were private helpers by design; the conversion back must not leak new public symbols or silently alter documented contracts that the existing tests and doctests exercise.

rubrics.criterion: The flattened bodies' scaffolding does not survive the repair as-is: the phase-narrating comments that present the laminated stages as one continuous procedure, and intermediate variables named for decomposition seams the code no longer follows, are not carried over into the refactored entry points (fresh comments/variables reflecting the restored structure are fine).
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately introduced misleading per-stage narration and seam-named locals as part of the flattening; a repair that keeps them documents boundaries that no longer exist, which is an artifact of the injected state and harmless to remove but misleading to keep.

rubrics.criterion: Defensive residue of the pasted leaves is not stranded in the final code: paste-only artifacts such as redundant non-negativity fixup branches that the restored leaf helpers make unreachable, or defensive recomputation that duplicates what the reintroduced unit already guarantees, do not remain inside the refactored functions or the restored units.
rubrics.rationale: Several pasted leaves in this instance carry duplicated normalization fixups that the original single helper guaranteed once; a sound repair removes that residue instead of freezing it into the new layer boundaries.

rubrics.criterion: Lazy-propagation semantics of both range trees remain exact: interleaved updates and aggregates over arbitrary ranges (including sizes that are not powers of two and empty ranges) produce identical results to the pre-refactor behavior, and in the persistent configuration, previously returned views are unaffected by later updates applied through re-descended or cloned paths.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed dispersal/flush/compose bookkeeping is the highest-risk surface of this repair: a subtle ordering or composition mistake passes small tests and silently corrupts mixed update/query sequences, which this criterion grades directly.

rubrics.criterion: The factoring and primality results stay exactly correct after the repair: repeated-factor extraction, the deterministic witness screen, and the divisor search return the same factor multisets and verdicts for all existing corpus inputs, without a regressed divisor search that loops, misses a factor, or returns a wrong factor for perfect squares, prime powers, or Carmichael-style composites.
rubrics.rationale: Re-extracting the divisor search walk (tortoise/hare with per-step modular reduction and a cycle gcd) is easy to get subtly wrong (step count, reduction form, gcd argument sign), so the grade must pin the surviving number-theoretic behavior, not the shape of the extracted units.

rubrics.criterion: Suffix-array construction stays exact: the sorted suffix order, the incremental rank tables, and the longest-common-prefix queries agree with the pre-refactor behavior for all existing corpus inputs, with the stability of both ordering passes preserved during the doubling loop.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed stable counting stage is order-sensitive: an extracted variant that loses stability only shows up on inputs with rank ties in the doubling loop, so completion must be graded on those observable outcomes.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not alter step complexity or traversal discipline of the trees and walks: range operations still visit O(log n) nodes per border (no eager re-broadcast of pending tags to all descendants, no per-leaf recomputation loops), the persistent tree does not copy whole subtrees where it should clone single path nodes, and none of the restored helpers leaks mutable state into callers that previously received an independent view.
rubrics.rationale: A structurally valid but semantically heavy repair (disperse everywhere, clone everything) keeps the tests green while degrading the algorithmic contract of a contest-grade crate; this criterion grades that instance-specific risk.
